correctness.rationale: For \(u=-\log(1-|\omega|^2)\), Wirtinger differentiation gives \(u_z=\overline\omega\,\omega'/(1-|\omega|^2)\) and \(\Delta u=4|\omega'|^2/(1-|\omega|^2)^2\). The holomorphic logarithmic derivative \(h''/h'\) has zero first positive Fourier mode. Circular averaging gives \(-r-(1-r^2)U'(r)/4\), and the divergence theorem gives \(U'(r)=2E/(\pi r)\), proving the coefficient \((1-r^2)/(2\pi r)\). The shear \(h(z)=z,\omega(z)=az\) saturates the sharp circlewise bound for every radius and nonzero slope. The 2026 criterion would give \(|A_f|\le 1/4\) for nonconstant dilatation, contradicting the circlewise bound at \(r=1/2\). For constant dilatation the criterion reduces to \(S_h=0\), hence a Möbius analytic part. Exact rational model checks were executed; the infinite theorem is established analytically.

value.rationale: The first angular Fourier coefficient is a canonical radial invariant of the harmonic order operator. An exact hyperbolic dilatation-energy remainder supplies sharp information at every radius, well beyond the scalar global order bound, and detects nonconstant dilatation. It also explains rigidity for a naturally formulated 2026 Schwarzian criterion. The quantified identity is the mathematical contribution; the classification consequence alone would not establish novelty or value. The claim is a structural formula for all locally univalent harmonic disk maps.
